newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM's party has narrow edge over opposition.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM's party has narrow edge over opposition.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) is maintaining a slim lead over the opposition Social Democrats a month before nationwide Senate elections, an opinion poll released on Monday showed.
The poll, conducted by the state-run Institute for Public Opinion Research (IVVM), gave Klaus's centre-right party 27 percent support, up two points from an IVVM poll in September.
The centre-left Social Democrats (CSSD) also gained support, edging up to 25 percent from 24 percent in the previous poll.
Another poll taken in September by the private Factum agency also showed the two parties running neck-and-neck, but with the CSSD holding a fractional advantage over the ODS.

Elections for the Senate, the upper house of the Czech parliament, will be held for the first time in the country's history on November 15 and 16 under a first-past-the-post system in 81 constituencies.
In parliamentary elections to the lower house in June, CSSD performed strongly to trail the ODS by just over three percent, depriving the government of a majority in the 200-seat house.

The IVVM poll showed that one of Klaus's coalition partners, the Christian Democrats, had slipped slightly to nine percent from a previous 11 percent. The Civic Democratic Alliance, another coalition member, held steady at eight percent.
The poll showed the Communist Party also at nine percent while the far-right Republican Party would not pass the five percent threshold necessary to take seats in the chamber.
